title: Case: A recipient logged that he was home five minutes after tracking recorded a no-answer attempt
context: DL-974 was booked for an evening window of 17:00 to 22:00 on 14 April. Tracking shows a failed attempt at 19:41.
initial_request: Hello. I want to set this out properly because I don't think anyone has actually read it. 1) My window was 17:00 to 22:00 on the 14th. 2) At 19:41 tracking said the driver called and nobody was home. 3) At 19:46, five minutes later, I wrote in your chat that I was in and nobody had come. I did that on purpose so there would be a time on it. 4) My doorbell logs every press. There is nothing between 18:10 and 21:30. 5) On the phone today I was told the drivers have GPS so it must have happened. Fine. Then could somebody please look at the GPS? That is all I am asking. I'm not trying to get anyone into trouble. I just want the parcel, and I don't want to take another evening off work for the same thing to happen.

events.body: Automated notice. DL-974 attempt 14 April 19:41. Driver note: 'called at address, no answer, card left'. Next attempt: not scheduled.

Logging this now so there is a record. It is 19:46. I am at home at 8 Corran Yard and have been since 16:30. The hall light is on. Nobody has rung the bell or knocked. Tracking has just changed to 'no answer'. There is no card.

Recipient explains he was home throughout the window and logged it in the portal at 19:46. Agent: 'Our drivers are GPS tracked, sir, so if it says he attended then he attended.' Recipient asks whether anyone has looked at the GPS for 19:41. Agent: 'I don't have that screen.' Line quality poor; recipient asks the agent to repeat himself three times. Call ends. No reference given.

DL-974: we stand by the driver note. Stop-level location records aren't visible to tracking support. Only Delivery investigations can pull them, on an emailed request quoting the attempt time. Rebooking is Scheduling's, and they won't rebook while an attempt is in dispute.

acceptable_actions.summary: Ask Delivery investigations to pull the stop-level location record for the 19:41 attempt on DL-974, setting out the driver note against the recipient's 19:46 record.

must: Sets out both accounts without choosing one: the driver note at 19:41 ('called at address, no answer, card left') and the recipient's portal entry at 19:46 that he was home, nobody had called and there was no card, with his doorbell log showing no press
Asks Delivery investigations to pull the stop-level location record for the 19:41 attempt on 14 April

Tells the team that nobody has yet checked that record and that the recipient was told by phone the attempt must be genuine because drivers are GPS-tracked, so they know he has already been brushed off once
must_not: Tells the recipient, or states to any team, that the attempt must have been genuine because drivers are tracked by GPS
States that the driver did not attend or falsified the attempt
Asks Scheduling to rebook, or promises the recipient a new delivery slot, while the attempt is in dispute
Sends the recipient a reply that only restates the driver note or says the carrier stands by it
expected.reference_message: Please review the attempt recorded on DL-974 at 19:41 on 14 April. The two accounts conflict. Driver note: 'called at address, no answer, card left'. The recipient was in a 17:00-22:00 window and logged in our portal at 19:46, five minutes later, that he was at home at 8 Corran Yard, that nobody had rung or knocked, and that there was no card. He also says his doorbell records presses and shows none between 18:10 and 21:30. Tracking support cannot see stop-level location and say only your team can pull it; nobody has looked yet. When he phoned on 15 April he was told the attempt must be genuine because drivers are GPS-tracked, without the record being checked. Could you pull the location record for that stop and time and tell me what it shows? I am not asserting either version. Scheduling will not rebook while this is open, so a reference and a first update time would help.

rationale: The driver's note and the recipient's timestamped portal entry contradict each other and the only record that can settle it has not been looked at. Tracking support has said that only Delivery investigations can pull it and that rebooking waits on the dispute. The desk should send the conflict there; telling him GPS proves the attempt, or telling anyone the driver lied, would both be deciding it without evidence.

review.note: Coordinator asked Delivery investigations by Email for the stop-level location record and set out both accounts without choosing one; matches the key.
